summary: Is the job worth it: The day after a crowd turns out against the town, {household member} asks whether the job is worth it.
realLife: One life: A Flint council president resigned because her health had suffered from the council's climate; she said meetings brought severe anxiety, she held back the news so as not to disrupt the budget vote, and her top priority became caring for herself with her family behind her. Another: Young state legislators said the job strained family life: one said his wife was pushing him to step away and he was thinking of leaving at 38, and another asked why he should put his family at risk. Events had to be planned and people were met at restaurants instead of at home. Another: A congressman and a former mayor said office strains families, that most members feel they spend too little time at home, and that one mayor moved her children to another school after a controversial vote. Both said the strain can strengthen or damage a family and the rewards were real. Another: A Rutgers researcher said local and legislative seats are often part-time and low-paid but feel full-time, hard on parents of young children; a founder of a mothers' group said campaign funds for child care open the door for more mothers.
gates: The civic record shows a strike or protest against the town's term in recent days.
{household member} lives with the player on the household record.
The player holds an office on {the body}.
weights: How large and how angry the crowd was.
How often the player is away at night.
Whether the pay of the office is low.
Whether a child is in the house.
How the household has felt about the job before.
choices: say why you hold the job and what it has done
say it looks worse than it is
promise time at home and name a night
say you cannot talk about it tonight

branches.when: the player says why they hold the job
branches.then: The household hears the reason; the tie warms if the reason is plain, and cools if it sounds like a speech.

branches.when: the player says it looks worse than it is
branches.then: The household reads the answer against what they saw; the gap is remembered.

branches.when: the player promises time at home
branches.then: The promise is written on the household record and kept or broken by later nights.

branches.when: the player puts the talk off
branches.then: The question stays open and is asked again after the next night meeting.
The support is written as a favor owed and may be said at the next race.
